text.p: U.S. fast-food giant McDonald's Corp opened on Monday what it said was the world's first ski-through restaurant.

At "McSki", located in the popular Swedish ski resort of Lindvallen about 450 km northwest of Stockholm, skiers order hamburgers and French fries through a special window and ski off, munching as they go.
The restaurant, which also has indoor seating for about 140 people, is some 100 metres from the resort's main ski lift, which can carry about 3,000 people an hour.

"The idea for the ski-through was actually under the theme of being where our customers are. Our guests decide where we should be," said Swedish McDonald's spokesman Bjorn Kallstrom at the opening ceremony for McSki.
Kallstrom said McDonald's aims to have 200 restaurants in Sweden by the year 2000, up from 120 today.
"We have discussed a goal of about 200 restaurants in the year 2000. If we find the sites we see that we can easily have that number of restaurants," Kallstrom told Reuters.
McDonald's employs some 7,000 people in Sweden and hires about 1,000 persons every year.
Kallstrom said McSki has aroused interest from McDonald's companies in other countries as well.
"We don't have any plans for more ski-throughs in Sweden, but who knows what will happen in the future," he said.
McDonald's fare is an alternative to higher-priced restaurants in the family-oriented resort of Lindvallen which is the sole listed ski resort on the Stockholm stock exchange, he said.
"That's part of the reason people wanted to have us. Lindvallen has a family profile, and the family is our main guest profile," Kallstrom said.
McDonald's has about 1.3 restaurants per 100,000 inhabitants in Sweden, which is about the European average, Kallstrom said.
McDonald's Swedish turnover is expected to rise to around two billion crowns ($292 million) in 1996 from 1.7 billion crowns the year before.
The company opened 26 new stores this year at more conventional McDonald's sites such as cities, shopping malls and drive-throughs.
There are 292 restaurants in the Nordic region, which includes Sweden, Denmark, Norway and Finland, Kallstrom said.
Worldwide McDonald's has more than 19,200 restaurants in 94 countries.
